title: Region-aware safety-descend fallback policy for pinned models
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently allow customers to pin model versions for stability, but our existing fallback behavior is brittle: when a pinned variant is unavailable in a region (capacity outage, GPU failure, or rolling deprecation), requests either fail or fall back to an uncontrolled variant with mismatched architecture/quantization, causing latency spikes and quality regressions. This ticket defines a compatibility-first, region-aware ‘safety-descend’ fallback policy to ensure graceful degradation of pinned versions while preserving SLA and output quality guarantees.

Goals:
- Define deterministic fallback ordering that considers region, model architecture compatibility, quantization compatibility, and performance profile.
- Implement deprecation windows and explicit migration signals to customers (and internal routing) rather than opaque silent swaps.
- Provide telemetry and traceability (audit log entries, rollout IDs) for every automated fallback decision.
- Add tooling to simulate fallback scenarios to validate fallbacks in staging and enable customers to run compatibility checks.

Scope & constraints:
- Works for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments (fallbacks in Private must not violate customer network boundaries).
- Must be SLO-aware: prefer options that keep latency and tail-latency within configured targets; degrade throughput before increasing 99th percentile latency.
- Compatibility checks must be fast and cached (no per-request heavyweight model metadata fetch).

Non-goals:
- Automating cross-region model transfers for Private deployments.
- Replacing customer-driven pin removal/migration workflows (we will communicate and provide migration tools, not force-push changes).
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic fallback graph is defined that ranks fallback candidates by (1) regional availability, (2) ABI/quantization compatibility, (3) performance-profile delta, (4) semantic-regression risk metadata.
Routing layer exposes a safety-descend mode flag that can be enabled per-customer and per-route.
When a pinned model becomes unavailable in a region, requests are routed according to the policy and produce audit log entries with the fallback reason and chosen variant ID.
Deprecation windows are surfaced to customers via notification and a pinned-version grace period (configurable), and internal routing honors the deprecation timeline for automatic weight decay.
We add a chaotic-staging harness that can simulate region outage + variant removal and validate fallback choices end-to-end (PR with tests merged).
Telemetry dashboards show fallback counts, average delta in per-token latency, and quality regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.
decisions: Policy will prefer same-architecture compatible quantized variant in the same region over cross-region lower-latency options.
If no compatible variant exists in-region, prefer regional replica of a compatible family. Cross-region routing requires explicit customer opt-in for Private deployments.
Deprecations will use a two-phase approach: NOTICE (30d) and FORCED-REDIRECT (configurable 7-14d) unless customer sets longer grace period.
Fallback choices must include a compatibility score and a human-readable reason placed in audit logs and customer-facing events.
rollout_plan: 1) Design doc and decision review (this ticket) -> 2) Implement policy engine + schema for compatibility metadata and grace windows -> 3) Add audit logging and expose route-level flag -> 4) Integrate with publish pipeline so onboarding includes compatibility metadata for every version -> 5) End-to-end staging tests with chaotic harness -> 6) Gradual rollout: internal-only, then beta customers, then global opt-in, then opt-out-by-default after 2 months if stability metrics are green.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: making cross-region fallbacks default improves availability but increases egress cost and could violate data locality for Private customers. We will default to region-local fallbacks and require explicit opt-in for cross-region routing for Private/VPC customers. We also debated a full semantic regression detector before fallback; due to time constraints we will rely on precomputed regression risk tags during onboarding and surface a flag for strict-eval customers.
